shorts.title: What you will learn: set and unordered_set
shorts.hook: Remove every duplicate in one line.
shorts.script: Remove every duplicate in one line. Today we meet the set. It stores each value once. It is the quickest way to remove duplicates. A set stores unique values. If you insert a value twice, the second insert does nothing. A set keeps its values sorted. An unordered set is faster, but it has no order. Insert returns a pair. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: set and unordered_set.

shorts.title: set and unordered_set in one minute
shorts.script: A set stores unique values. If you insert a value twice, the second insert does nothing. A set keeps its values sorted. An unordered set is faster, but it has no order. Insert returns a pair. The second part tells you if the value was new. Think of a guest list. Every name appears once, and the clerk keeps it in order. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: set and unordered_set in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.script: The first insert adds four. The second insert finds four already there. The second part of the result is a flag. The first flag is true, and the second is false. Count tells us if a value is in the set. Four is there, so one. Seven is not, so zero. The program prints true false, and then one zero. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: Expecting duplicates
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in set and unordered set?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in set and unordered set? Bug of the Day. We count six ballots, but the program says three. A set keeps each value once. It counts the different candidates, not the votes. Use a vector, or a map of counts, when duplicates matter. A set keeps each value once, so it counts the different values, not the total. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: Expecting duplicates.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you remove the duplicates from a vector in set
shorts.script: Can you remove the duplicates from a vector in set and unordered set? A set told a joke twice. Nobody heard it the second time. Read five numbers into a vector. Print them without duplicates, in sorted order. Write your answer in the comments. A set stores each value once. A set keeps its values sorted. Insert tells you if the value was new. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
